test_case: Master program starts on Raspberry Pi
expected_result: The 3.5 inch LCD shows the name entry screen or waiting screen.
actual_result: The LCD showed the expected screen.
comment: This test verifies that the Master software can start and that the LCD output is working.

expected_result: The Client starts without a display and waits/sends controller messages to the Master.
actual_result: The Client started without a display.
comment: This confirms the requirement that the second SBC is used without a display during operation.

expected_result: The Master detects the Client connection after the Client program starts.
comment: The Master and Client were connected over Wi-Fi/WLAN using UDP communication.

expected_result: The player changes direction to UP when B7 is pressed on the Master controller.
comment: Master controller input for UP direction was verified.

expected_result: The player changes direction to LEFT when B8 is pressed on the Master controller.
comment: Master controller input for LEFT direction was verified.

test_case: B4 yellow button: Enter / next field
expected_result: The virtual keyboard moves to the next input field when B4 is pressed.
comment: This button is used during team/player name entry.

expected_result: The selected keyboard character is added to the active name field when B5 is pressed.
comment: B5 was used instead of B6 because the schematic clearly provides a shared ground for Button 4-5.

test_case: B1 green button: start / play again
expected_result: The game starts or restarts when B1 is pressed in the correct menu state.
comment: The button was tested in the start/result menu states.

expected_result: The game can be reset or moved to the result screen depending on the current state.
comment: This function is useful for restarting the test without rebooting the Raspberry Pi.

expected_result: The player changes direction to DOWN after the Client sends the DOWN command.
comment: This verifies that Client-side input is received by the Master.

expected_result: The player changes direction to RIGHT after the Client sends the RIGHT command.
comment: This verifies that the Client is responsible for RIGHT movement.

expected_result: After a direction is selected, the player continues moving in the last selected direction.
actual_result: The player continued moving in the last direction.
comment: This matches the game requirement that the player keeps moving in the last direction.

expected_result: A random maze is generated and displayed on the Master LCD.
actual_result: A maze was generated and displayed.
comment: The maze generation was checked visually on the LCD.

expected_result: The game ends when the player reaches the finish field.
actual_result: The game ended at the finish field.
comment: The finish condition was verified by reaching the target cell.

expected_result: The score or star counter changes after collecting a star.
comment: This verifies that collectible objects affect the game result.

expected_result: The monster hit counter increases after collision with the monster.
comment: The result screen was checked after a monster collision.

expected_result: The hole hit counter increases after falling into a hole.
comment: The result screen was checked after a hole collision.

expected_result: The result screen shows score, stars, monster hits, hole hits, duration, latency, and packet errors.
actual_result: The result screen displayed the required game data.
comment: The result screen is used to verify the final game and measurement data.

expected_result: The result screen shows Master status such as CPU, RAM, temperature, uptime, and software/build information.
comment: This verifies that diagnostic information of the first SBC is visible.

expected_result: The result screen shows Client status such as connection state, latency, packet errors, and reported system information.
comment: This verifies that the second SBC status is included in the final visualization.

expected_result: The file maze_scores.csv is created or updated after the game ends.
actual_result: The CSV file was created/updated and was readable.
comment: This file is the main machine-readable measurement output of the game.

expected_result: The CSV file contains timestamp, team/player names, score, duration, latency, and packet error fields.
actual_result: The CSV file contained the expected fields.
comment: The CSV columns were checked to ensure that the required measurement data is stored.

expected_result: If the Client or network is interrupted, the Master detects missing Client messages or the Client status changes.
actual_result: The connection status changed or Client movement stopped.
comment: This test checks communication-loss behavior. If not fully tested, change status to NOT TESTED.

expected_result: Released buttons do not trigger repeated false input events.
actual_result: No false input was observed after button release.
comment: This checks button debounce and stable GPIO input behavior.

expected_result: The game is shown on the 3.5 inch LCD connected to the Master Raspberry Pi.
actual_result: The game was visible on the LCD.
comment: The Master LCD was tested using the framebuffer output on /dev/fb1.

expected_result: The Client Raspberry Pi runs without a display during the game.
actual_result: The Client was used without a display.
comment: Only the Master has the central display; the Client is used as a headless controller device.
